title: Deploy hybrid anomaly detection service for console metrics (usage / cost / latency)
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build and deploy a hybrid anomaly detection service for Console backend usage, cost, and latency metrics. The service will combine lightweight statistical baselines (EWMA + seasonal decomposition) with a low-latency ML detector (online Isolation Forest / streaming model) to surface actionable anomalies per-customer, per-route, and per-model. Alerts should be deduplicated, rate-limited, and include contextual metadata (last-known rollout, model id, region, recent errors, token breakdowns) so SREs/PMs can quickly triage. The feature spans real-time streaming detection, batch backfill/retraining, and Console alerting UI integrations.
problem_statement: We currently have manual thresholds and ad-hoc anomaly scripts for console metrics. This leads to noisy alerts, slow detection of regressions (e.g., spike in per-token latency after kernel change), and limited ability to correlate cost anomalies with model rollouts or routing changes. Customers and internal teams miss regressions or get swamped by false positives.
goals: Detect statistically-significant deviations in usage, cost, and tail/median latency within 2 minutes of occurrence for high-volume customers
Provide per-customer and per-route anomaly scoring with root-cause hints (recent deployments, model switches, region outages)
Reduce noisy alerts via adaptive thresholds, dedup windows, and simple severity scoring
Integrate alerts into Console (notifications + incident creation) and Ops channels (Slack/PagerDuty)
Support backfill reprocessing and baseline recalculation for post-mortem analysis
non_goals: Full-blown blackbox deep learning models for anomaly detection (out of scope for initial rollout)
Automatic remediation for anomalies (only detection + guidance in this ticket)
Changing existing billing computation logic (we use present billing events as input, not recalculating cost)
technical_design: Data sources: console.metrics.raw topic(s) in Kafka (usage events, billing events, per-token latency traces aggregated at ingestion), plus model-rollout events and deployment metadata from console.audit and runtime events

Preprocessing: stream-enrichment Flink job reads console.metrics.raw -> normalizes keys, aggregates 1m/5m windows, computes features: count, p50/p95/p99 latency, token_count, cost_sum, error_rate, cold_start_rate, and recent model_id/route_id labels

Baseline layer: ClickHouse (or BigQuery for longer retention) stores historical aggregates. Baseline service computes EWMA and seasonal decomposition per entity (customer/route/model) and exposes an HTTP API used by the online detector for thresholding

ML detector: lightweight online Isolation Forest (or streaming LOF) implemented in the Flink job using incremental feature vector windowing. The detector emits anomaly_score and anomaly_type (usage_spike, cost_spike, latency_tail) with confidence bands

Hybrid decision logic: anomalies are raised if (score > threshold) AND (deviation > baseline_multiplier). Baseline_multiplier adapted by entity volume class (low volume uses higher multiplier to avoid noise).

Dedup & suppression: stateful dedup window (default 30m) per entity+anomaly_type. Severity levels: warn, critical based on magnitude and customer tier (reserved capacity customers escalate faster), with automatic backoff for repeat alerts

Alert sinks: console-alerts topic -> Alerting service routes to Console UI (in-app banners), Slack Ops channel, and PagerDuty. Alerts include contextual links to: model rollout dashboard, Trace/Span links, recent PRs (via GitHub webhook matching recent deploys), and cost breakdown link
Backfill & retrain: Airflow DAG to reprocess historical windows, recompute baselines, and allow tuning thresholds. This DAG can replay Kafka partitions to regenerate detector inputs for post-mortems
Operational telemetry: instrument detector latency, false-positive rate (via manual ack/unack in Console), processed events/s, and storage of anomalies in ClickHouse for ad-hoc queries

Data privacy: billing and usage events may contain customer IDs. All output stored in internal-only namespaces; PII fields are redacted. Access controlled via Console RBAC and requires security review prior to GA
data_pipeline_changes: Flink streaming job: metrics-enrich + feature-extract + detector operator
Baseline service: periodic batch job writing EWMA/seasonality metadata into ClickHouse tables
Airflow DAG: anomaly-backfill-reprocess -> triggers recompute of baselines and replay of detection for specified time ranges
Schema versioning: bump metrics event schema (avro) to include model_id, route_id, and billing_token_bucket_id
alerting_logic: Severity calculation: combine anomaly_score, relative deviation from baseline, and customer_tier to compute severity
Suppression policy: initial alert, then suppress identical alerts for 30m; if anomaly persists and severity increases, escalate
Grouping: group by customer_id + affected_entity (route/model) with top-K affected routes included in the alert payload
Noise controls: minimum volume thresholds per-entity to avoid triggering on sparse entities; heartbeat checks to detect emitter failures
Enrichment: attach last 10min token-level cost/latency breakdown, recent deploy ID, region, and suggested next steps
acceptance_criteria: Real-time detection: high-volume customer anomaly detected and emitted within 2 minutes in >95% of synthetic test runs
False positive rate: fewer than 5% noise rate on controlled synthetic baseline tests for tiered customers
End-to-end: an alert created in Console and routed to Slack + PagerDuty with contextual links for at least 3 test scenarios (usage spike, cost anomaly, latency tail)
Backfill: Airflow DAG can reprocess a 7-day window in <4 hours for a single cluster backfill cluster-size configuration
RBAC: only console-observability and SRE roles can view raw anomaly payloads; others see redacted summaries
Monitoring: detector and Flink job emit metrics and SLOs wired into current Prometheus/Grafana dashboards
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): deploy Flink reader + detector in a single region, run in shadow mode (no alerts) against production traffic for 2 weeks, compare with manual thresholds
Phase 1 (ops-only): enable alerts for internal Redwood teams only (SRE, Platform PMs) for 1 week
Phase 2 (select customers): opt-in group of 5 customers (mix of PLG and reserved) enable alerts and gather feedback
Phase 3 (GA): enable for all customers with default suppression policy and UI toggle in Console with clear allowlist for PagerDuty escalation
Rollback: ability to flip alerts to shadow or disable detector via feature flag and revert Kafka topic routing to queue-only processing
monitoring_and_sla: Pipeline health SLO: processing latency for 1m aggregates < 60s 99th percentile
Detector uptime: 99.9% for the Flink job (monitored via jobmanager metrics)
Alert delivery: 99% success to Slack/PagerDuty for generated alerts
Error budget policy: if false-positive rate exceeds threshold for 2 consecutive days, auto-disable customer-facing alerts and notify PM/Eng
